primitive.relation: four separate representations of the edges of a cyclic vertex sequence, all by conversion: X9 x9_cycle_edges, X24 x24_cycle_edge_seq and X25 x25_cycle_edge_seq are GTBase.walks_paths.seq_cycle_edge_list c (ordered list of the pairs of zip c (rot 1 c), closing pair included); X216 x216_cycle_edges is seq_cycle_edge_set c (its finite support); Cycle XE1 xe1_cycle_edges is seq_cycle_graph_edge_set c (the actual edges among those pairs, equal to seq_cycle_edge_set c :&: E(G) for every c); U2 cycle_edges, X211 x211_cycle_edges and U9 cycle_edgesG are seq_next_edge_set c (the first-occurrence successor image, contained in the support and equal to it under uniq c)

raw-ordered-list.note: map (fun p => [set p.1; p.2]) (zip c (rot 1 c)), the body of seq_cycle_edge_list c, convertible: one entry per position of c, the closing pair (last, first) included; order and multiplicity are kept (a two-entry sequence lists its pair twice, a one-entry sequence lists [set x]); no adjacency, uniqueness or length check. Rotation rotates the list and reversal reverses it up to a rotation by one, so it is invariant only up to perm_eq. X25's helper keeps its M1/C2 frozen copy (Packing.migration.simple_edges.X25Legacy).

raw-finite-support.note: X216's [set e | e \in [seq [set p.1; p.2] | p <- zip c (rot 1 c)]], the body of seq_cycle_edge_set c, convertible: membership in the raw list, so multiplicity is dropped while non-adjacent pairs and one-vertex sets [set x] are kept; it is not E(G). Invariant under rot, rotr and rev with no premise. X216's BLOCKED complexity row and its documented defect are unchanged.

actual-edge-filter.note: Cycle XE1's actual edges [set p.1; p.2] with p.1, p.2 in c, p.1 -- p.2 and (p.1, p.2) or (p.2, p.1) in zip c (rot 1 c): the body of seq_cycle_graph_edge_set c with seq_cyclic_consecutiveb's body, convertible. It equals seq_cycle_edge_set c :&: E(G) for every c (seq_cycle_graph_edge_setE) and the raw support under the sufficient guard cycle (--) c, without uniqueness (seq_cycle_graph_edge_set_cycle); a loop [:: x] or a non-adjacent pair contributes nothing.

first-occurrence-next-image.note: [set [set x; next c x] | x in [set z | z \in c]] (byte-identical in U2, X211 and U9), the body of seq_next_edge_set c, convertible; the explicit Arguments of the three helpers are kept. MathComp's next reads the FIRST occurrence: the image is contained in the raw support for every c and equal to it under the sufficient guard uniq c (seq_next_edge_set_uniq), hence equal to the actual edges on a ucycle; on the closed walk [:: 0; 1; 0; 2; 3] of K_4 it misses the edge {0, 2}, and rotating or reversing that sequence changes it. The Hamilton digon convention and empty-carrier behaviour are untouched: no length guard is added.

upstream_audit.note: MathComp path.v owns next (next_nth, mem_next, next_cycle) with prev_next, next_prev, next_rot, next_rotr and next_rev under a duplicate-free cycle; coq-graph-theory writes the edge set of a simple graph as E(G) (in_edges) and packages typed paths. Neither library names the cyclic edge list of a raw sequence, its support, its actual-edge filter or the first-occurrence successor image, so GTBase.walks_paths owns seq_cycle_edge_list, seq_cycle_edge_set, seq_cycle_graph_edge_set and seq_next_edge_set, with the public succession bridges seq_next_in_zip and seq_zip_nextE proved from next_nth (the Hom.conjectures.grounding_U3 lemmas were a design reference only, not imported). The open seq_edge_list / seq_edge_set (family path-edges) lack the closing pair and stay separate. Digraph P9 cyc_arcs (ordered successor arcs), Cycle U6 cyc_pairs (multigraph edge objects), Extremal X84 x84_cycle_edge_set (a predicate on an edge set, not an extractor; since B29 owned by family cycle-lengths, edge-family class), rainbow/colour sequences (Cycle X10, Chromatic U5), Digraph path_fas hits_cycle and Hom U3 chords stay separate; cycle vertex sets (Chromatic X153, Cycle X10/X212, Digraph X19) are a later path-vertices extension. Legacy bodies and per-row certificates: meta/migration_reports/cycle_edges.md.
